correctness.rationale: Direct classification of orbit maps proves fixed points cannot enter free orbits and every idempotent is a depth-one rooted forest. Separate free-source coordinate translations trivialize each free-to-free nonroot phase even for nonabelian G, giving complete orbit invariants. Labeled rooted-star factorial counting proves individual orbit size, and multiset Euler factors prove the rank polynomial. The attached standalone enumerator checked 33 actual finite equivariant-monid cases, class sizes, independent coefficients and generated unit orbits. It is a finite cross-check, not the proof for arbitrary G.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Arbitrary cycle-type labeled idempotent rank formula covers the total element counts after restricting to free and singleton cycles, but it is a sum of class sizes and cannot recover their partition by unit conjugacy. The relative-rank theorem is about generators, so has a different conclusion. Neither dominates the asserted quotient classification.

originality.rationale: Searches of published records, the finite G-set primary articles, relevant open thesis sections, and claim summaries in the accessible private mathematical ledger did not find the mixed fixed/free unit-conjugacy classification or the individual orbit formula. The 2022 framework establishes relative rank and orbit types; the homogeneous free G-act theorem normalizes labels on one orbit type; the 2018 thesis and permutation-centralizer work count labeled idempotents, which do not determine conjugacy orbits. A general historical orbit theorem could conceivably subsume this result and is retained as a priority risk; non-detection is not treated as proof of novelty.
residual_risks: Earlier general characterizations of finite G-set retractions up to G-set isomorphism, especially older semigroup species and table-of-marks literature, may imply the restricted two-type formula.
The published homogeneous gauge theorem gives a strong conceptual precedent, so the novelty is the mixed two-type orbit profile and exact sizes, not the phase-normalization idea by itself.

value.rationale: The quotient by all equivariant units is a canonical classification problem for retractions of heterogeneous finite G-sets. The complete all-dimensional mixed-isotropy orbit invariant and exact orbit-cardinality formula are substantively different from known labeled counts and homogeneous monoid enumerations. A group-independent orbit number despite strongly group-dependent labeled counts is a meaningful structural phenomenon, with direct use in studying intermediate stabilizer orbit types.
